- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at +3-4% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; add 1-2 days of upward correction.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above 18d history mean, reduce by 1-2% per day until convergence.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, sentiment-driven momentum is stronger than price history; prioritize sentiment alignment over technical trends.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 1-2% to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
